newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai exports seen growing only 7.0 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Thai exports seen growing only 7.0 pct in 1996.

text.p: Sluggish Thai exports were likely to grow only seven percent in 1996 against 23.6 percent in 1995, president of the Thai Bankers' Association said on Friday.
Olarn Chaipravat, who is also chief executive of Siam Commercial Bank Plc, said the remaining four months of 1996 left the Thai government little time to adopt new measures to bolster exports.
The banker made the statement during a break from a government-organised meeting to review ways of reviving slowing exports.
Figures released by the Bank of Thailand on Thursday showed that exports rose only 3.8 percent during the first seven months of this year against 26.2 percent in the same period of 1995.
Central bank officials said the sharp slowdown was mainly due to weak exports of electronics, computer parts, textile, and other manufactured products to the United States and Japan.
